## Trial `cron-access-control-rhel10__NHWNKxQ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow, created the missing opsadmin user, and directly verified both allow and deny behavior before and after a full node restart (with boot_id proving an actual reboot occurred). All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. Hygiene is good with only a minor leftover artifact (/tmp/reboot.log) and no unreverted unnecessary mutations.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 14/2 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Restrict cron scheduling on node1 to only root and opsadmin (via /etc/cron.allow or equivalent mechanism)
  - **Why:** Baseline showed no /etc/cron.allow and an empty /etc/cron.deny (all users permitted). Executor created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', created the missing opsadmin user, and directly verified enforcement: root and opsadmin can install crontabs while a disallowed test user (testuser) is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-381d3bfd8ce64a44`, `cmd-e602adf2969a4bfe`, `cmd-ea161006dd5f4373`, `cmd-e99966b9e1964fb1`, `cmd-f60a00db751045cb`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Restriction is durable/persistent (survives a service or system restart, not just an in-memory or ephemeral state)
  - **Why:** Executor captured pre-restart boot_id, triggered systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), confirmed boot_id changed from 21972395-... to 32e4f377-... proving an actual reboot, then re-verified post-restart that crond is active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin can still use crontab, and a newly created non-listed user (verifyuser) is still denied. This directly demonstrates the healthy pre-state, the restart, and the recovered/enforced state post-restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ef7433923ae74a5c`, `cmd-b5e0b714ab3e43e8`, `cmd-1f56d7425a564227`, `cmd-01b44d0bba7a4a63`, `cmd-70b76bb77702421d`, `cmd-ebb3fcbada4e4884`, `cmd-34b1e6a5edb84f2e`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** cron service (crond) remains healthy/active throughout and after the change
  - **Why:** crond reported active both before and after the restart, and no failed systemd units were observed in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ef7433923ae74a5c`, `cmd-70b76bb77702421d`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor commands were reviewed chronologically. Test users (testuser, verifyuser) were created solely to validate the access-control policy (a legitimate verification step) and were both removed afterward — testuser removal initially failed because a lingering process held the account (cmd-9402415d81ed4db1) but was cleaned up moments later via loginctl/pkill/userdel (cmd-21abfd9c8ac04200); verifyuser was removed in the same command that created it (cmd-ebb3fcbada4e4884) and confirmed absent (cmd-34b1e6a5edb84f2e). No unnecessary mutations were retained. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, created as a side effect of backgrounding the 'systemctl reboot' command (cmd-b5e0b714ab3e43e8), was left on the node and appears in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; it is low-risk (an empty/near-empty log file) but was not cleaned up. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, no package-state damage, and cron.deny was correctly left in place unmodified (harmless once cron.allow exists).

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9402415d81ed4db1`, `cmd-21abfd9c8ac04200`, `cmd-ebb3fcbada4e4884`, `cmd-34b1e6a5edb84f2e`, `cmd-b5e0b714ab3e43e8`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`
